blocks.text: Environment variables aren't access-controlled or encrypted: they're visible through the Docker API, /proc, every child process, logs and, if set at build time, the image itself.

rows: Config.Env in plain text to anyone with Docker access
`set -x`, debug pages, printing settings, error trackers
ENV or build ARGs in config/history

blocks.text: `set -x` in an entrypoint prints `psql "postgresql://app:${DB_PASSWORD}@db/rag"` fully expanded into your logs.

items: Dev/CI: env is acceptable; keep .env git-ignored and docker-ignored; commit .env.example.
Production: mounted secret files or a secret manager.
In code: SecretStr, never log settings, scrub error reports, don't pass the full env to subprocesses.

blocks.text: Q: "Why are environment variables considered unsafe for secrets?" A: "They show up in docker inspect, /proc, every child process, logs and CI output, and in the image if set at build time. Use them for non-sensitive config; deliver secrets as mounted files or via a secret manager, using the _FILE convention."

items: Build-time env ships in the image.
set -x and debug logging leak values.
Prefer files or secret managers in prod.
